title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are Grothendieck's hand computations, from about 1978 onward, of the automorphisms of profinite fundamental groupoids of genus-0 'Teichmüller' situations. The aim is to describe the Galois action, or more generally the 'Teichmüller-type' automorphisms, on the tower. The groupoids are taken with respect to several systems of base points on the Riemann sphere:
- P^ω: the two poles, ω = ±.
- Q_i: tangential points near 0, 1, ∞.
- R_i^ω: points on the meridians/equator.
Here π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, i.e. the free profinite group on two generators. Automorphisms are parametrized by elements λ, ξ', η, ... of π̂_{0,3}, entering through 'twisting' formulas such as u(d̃_i^ω) = φ_i^ω(ξ') d̃_i^ω, where the φ_i^ω are transport isomorphisms. σ_∞ is the involution of π̂_{0,3} exchanging 0 and 1 and fixing ∞; ρ is the order-3 rotation 0→1→∞.

Step 1, end of the sentence from p.37. Prescribing the automorphism on the generating arrows d̃_i^ω suffices, because its effect on the ã_i^ω is already determined by ξ.

Step 2, diagram (68). The groupoids I through VII, each the full subgroupoid on a different set of base points with its chosen generating graph, form an inclusion diagram:
- III includes into II and into IV;
- I ↪ II, I ↪ VII, II ↪ VI, VII ↪ VI;
- V ↪ IV, IV → VI.
I, II, VII, VI are boxed together. So the automorphism data on the different groupoids are compatible by restriction.

Step 3, groupoid VII. VII is the full subgroupoid on the eight vertices (R_i^ω, P^ω), generated by 24 arrows. Consider its automorphisms that fix each vertex and commute with σ_∞, the symmetry exchanging the two hemispheres. These correspond to triples (λ, β', ξ') ∈ π̂_{0,3}^3 subject to (70):
- β' = α' σ_∞(λ), with α' = ξ' ρ**(η')^{-1};
- β' σ_∞(β') = 1, equivalently α' σ_∞(λ) σ_∞(α') λ = 1.
Since β' is expressed through α' and λ, it is a redundant parameter ('donc β' inutile!').

Step 4, groupoid II. II is parametrized by (λ, η, α') subject to (70'):
- β' = α' σ_∞(λ);
- α' ρ(α') ρ²(α') = 1;
- with β' = η σ_∞(η)^{-1}.
Now α' = β' σ_∞(λ)^{-1} is determined, hence 'donc α' inutile!'.

In modern terms, the conditions x·σ(x) = 1 and x·ρ(x)·ρ²(x) = 1 are exactly the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations that define the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂. Drinfeld later wrote them as f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1. They arise here from the requirement that automorphisms of profinite genus-0 groupoids with several base points be compatible with the symmetries σ and ρ. The page thus shows Grothendieck deriving the GT-type defining relations by a 'Lego' computation with explicit groupoids and base-point systems. The next page (21) passes to genus 2 [?] with generators (71) and relations (72)–(75).
errors: No mathematical error detected. Check of (70): with σ_∞ an involution, β'σ_∞(β') = α'σ_∞(λ)·σ_∞(α')λ, which matches the 'i.e.' form.
In (70') the parametrization β' = ησ_∞(η)^{-1} automatically satisfies β'σ_∞(β') = 1. So the 2-cycle condition is built into the parametrization rather than imposed, which is consistent.
The exponent in 'ρ**(η')^{-1}' is illegible; it is probably ρ^{-1} or ρ^2. Its exact value cannot be verified from this page.
Only the relations are listed. No claim of completeness (that these relations characterize the automorphisms) is proved on this page; 'je puis déjà préciser' signals a preliminary result.

ideas.what: Diagram (68): inclusions among profinite fundamental groupoids of the sphere with different base-point systems (I–VII), used to propagate automorphisms by restriction
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller groupoid / 'Lego' with tangential base points; compatibility of GT-actions under restriction to subgroupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) as program; Drinfeld 1990; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§2, Teichmüller tower and 'jeu de Lego'), in general form only, without these computations

ideas.what: Automorphisms of groupoid VII that fix vertices and commute with σ_∞ ⇔ triples (λ, β', ξ') with β'σ_∞(β') = 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990–91) for the profinite version

ideas.what: For groupoid II, the condition α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1 with β' = ησ_∞(η)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon) relation of GT̂, combined with a 'coboundary' parametrization of 2-cycle solutions

ideas.what: Elimination of redundant parameters ('β' inutile', 'α' inutile') when the automorphism is presented on different generating graphs
ideas.modern_name: choice of minimal generating data for automorphisms of groupoids (change of base-point system)

missed.claim: An explicit, pre-Drinfeld manuscript derivation of the 2-cycle relation β'σ_∞(β') = 1 and the 3-cycle relation α'ρ(α')ρ²(α') = 1 for automorphisms of profinite genus-0 groupoids. They come out of a systematic comparison of groupoids with different base-point sets, linked by inclusion diagram (68). The Esquisse states only the program; this page contains the actual equations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the defining relations of GT̂, or close equivalents, in explicit form in his Teichmüller notes from about 1978–84. That bears on historical attribution of the GT relations, which are usually dated to Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara.

missed.claim: Imposing compatibility with σ_∞ (a symmetry exchanging hemispheres, i.e. poles P^+ and P^-) on groupoids with tangential points on the equator suggests the relations can be derived via 'real structure'/reflection symmetry of the sphere decomposition. This resembles later work on GT acting on groupoids with real or dihedral symmetry (e.g. GT and real structures, dihedral moduli spaces), but the precise route via VII is not standard.
missed.quote: le domaine des automorphismes de VII fixant les sommets et commutant à σ_∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give an alternative presentation of GT̂ through an 8-vertex groupoid with 24 generating arrows. It is worth comparing with Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and with the dihedral/real versions of GT.

missed.claim: The text says 'je puis déjà préciser', and p.21 moves to computations [?] 'en genre deux'. The full determination of automorphisms of VI and of the whole diagram (68), including the λ-twists, is left open on this page.
missed.quote: Sur calcul, je puis déjà préciser que …
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Completing the computation would show whether Grothendieck's system of groupoids I–VII yields exactly GT̂ or a variant, such as a subgroup cut out by extra relations from the λ-twists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains explicit GT-type 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations in Grothendieck's own notation, years before Drinfeld. It also has a concrete inclusion diagram of base-point groupoids. Specialists suspect Grothendieck had such computations, but the explicit form is not in the published record. The material is still preliminary and partly illegible, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'respire les u(ã_i^ω), résulte déjà de celle de ξ' — the word 'résulte' is struck through in the image. The construction reads roughly '[la donnée de ξ] respire les u(ã_i^ω), déjà de celle de ξ, qui respire les u(d̃_i^ω)'.
'Sur, calcul' is likely 'Sur calcul' or 'Par calcul'.
'équivaut à le domaine' is probably 'équivaut au domaine' or 'équivaut à la donnée'.
In (70), 'ρ**(η')' has an unclear superscript, possibly ρ^{-1} or ρ^2.
Diagram (68): the arrow from II to the right is a double-headed/struck arrow. IV → VI goes from IV to VI (lower right), and V ↪ IV is drawn as a hook arrow from V to IV.
